newsitem.title: USA: Continental, pilots far apart on new pact.
newsitem.headline: Continental, pilots far apart on new pact.

text.p: On the eve of the first round of contract negotiations between Continental Airlines Inc. and its pilots union, the two sides remained far apart on most major issues, the pilots said Wednesday.

The union, which is seeking an "industry standard" contract that would include a 38 percent wage increase and work concessions, said the airline gave little ground in an initial proposal presented to the pilots last week.

"In 19 of 25 sections, there is either no change or a minor change proposed by the company," said Bill Borrelli, a vice president of the Independent Association of Continental Pilots. "We're not alarmed by it necessarily, but it indicates they want to stay pat on most sections of the contract."

Negotiators with the Houston-based airline, the nation's fifth-largest, and its 5,000-member pilots union were set to open talks in Washington on Thursday, one week after exchanging initial contract proposals.

Continental has pledged to boost the pay of its pilots, who agreed to wage concessions in an initial 1992 contract as the carrier navigated its way out of bankruptcy and went on to become one of the strongest domestic airlines.
"Our pilots deserve more pay, and we plan to pay them more -- just like we've done with all other employees during the past year," Continental spokesman Ned Walker said.

The Continental pilots' labour agreement expires June 30, and both sides have said they expect to forge a new pact covering both Continental and its sibling regional airline, Continental Express, before the deadline.

Continental's pilots are seeking a 38 percent increase in salaries that would bring their wages in line with pilots at the nation's five largest airlines. The union also proposed improvements in its retirement plan and scheduling changes.
The company in its initial proposal did not put new salary figures on the table, Borrelli said. "There is no specific pay proposal," he said.

Both the company and union negotiators declined to discuss other issues up for negotiation. "We don't anticipate making any public comments on the specifics of the negotiations since those are best left at the bargaining table," Walker said.
In separate talks, negotiators meeting in Atlanta on Monday reached tentative agreement on several "non-economic sections" of a new pact between Continental Express and its 1,000 pilots.
